statements.impact_statement: Expires: 2026-12-02. Surface: website/package-lock.json only; path website -> astro@7.3.3 (dependencies) -> http-cache-semantics ^4.2.0; no other consumer in the lockfile. No fix exists: 4.2.0 is the latest release, the advisory range is <= 4.2.0 with first_patched_version null, and the upstream fix (kornelski/http-cache-semantics PR #58) is open and unmerged. The vulnerable path is CachePolicy.satisfiesWithoutRevalidation() honouring a client-supplied Cache-Control: max-stale on a shared-cache entry whose maxAge() was zeroed for Set-Cookie / proxy-revalidate, which lets one client read another client's cached response. In astro the module is imported by exactly one file, dist/assets/build/remote.js, which only calls policy.storable() and policy.timeToLive() on a Request astro constructs itself (new Request(src), no client headers) while fetching REMOTE images for astro:assets during the static build; nothing in astro/dist/runtime, astro/dist/core/app or @astrojs/node references it, so it is never loaded by the Node adapter process that serves the prerendered site. The site itself never reaches even that build-time code: website/src has no astro:assets import (no <Image>/<Picture>/getImage()) and astro.config.mjs declares no image.domains / image.remotePatterns, so no remote image is ever fetched. Re-evaluate on expiry, when astro bumps or drops the dependency, or when a patched http-cache-semantics (> 4.2.0) is published (then bump via an npm override instead of extending this statement).
